planting.note: Root hardwood cuttings in late winter or set out container plants in spring after frost danger passes; give it full sun and good drainage.

directions: Black Ischia is a small-to-medium fig with near-black, purple-black skin that lacks a pronounced neck, opening to reveal strawberry-pink to red flesh with a rich, sweet flavor. Long grown on the Mediterranean island of Ischia and popularized in American gardens through heirloom fruit exchanges, it typically bears both a light early breba crop and a heavier main crop in warm climates. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil and prune lightly in winter to maintain an open, easily harvested framework, since the thin skin bruises readily. It is valued by home growers for its rich flavor rather than shipping quality, making it best suited to dooryard planting rather than commercial production.

planting.note: Root cuttings indoors in late winter or plant out container stock in spring; site against a warm, sheltered wall in marginal climates to boost heat accumulation.

directions: An English heirloom selected for reliability in cool, short-season climates, Preston's Prolific produces medium-sized, brown-purple fruit with sweet amber flesh and is prized for setting a dependable breba crop even where summer heat is limited. Plant in full sun against a south-facing wall or in a warm microclimate to maximize ripening in marginal areas, and mulch the root zone well for winter protection. It fruits readily on both old and new wood, so light annual pruning to remove crossing branches is usually all that's needed. This cultivar is a good choice for gardeners in cooler temperate regions who want fruit without a heated greenhouse.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; expect a light breba crop in early summer followed by the main crop in late summer.

directions: Atreano is a Portuguese fig notable for its pale yellow-green skin that stays light even when the fruit is fully ripe, which makes judging harvest timing by color alone unreliable; instead check for softening and a slight neck droop. The amber flesh is mild, honeyed, and low in seediness, making it a favorite for fresh eating among growers who find darker figs too intensely flavored. It is a vigorous, heavy-bearing tree well suited to warm Mediterranean-type and humid subtropical climates alike. Give it full sun, good drainage, and room to spread, since it can become a large, dense specimen if left unpruned.

planting.note: Plant cutting-grown stock in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; it ripens its main crop mid-to-late season, so it suits regions with a long, warm growing season.

directions: A classic fig of Provence, Bourjassotte Grise bears medium-sized fruit with a distinctive grayish-brown to violet-tinted skin covering deep strawberry-red flesh with a rich, sweet, complex flavor long prized in French markets. The tree is moderately vigorous and reliably productive once established, generally favoring a single strong main crop over a heavy breba crop. Plant in full sun with good air circulation, since the thin skin is prone to splitting after heavy rain near harvest. It is best suited to long, warm-summer climates where the late-season fruit has time to fully ripen before cool weather arrives.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or rooted-cutting stock in spring in full sun; it reliably sets both a breba and a main crop in warm climates, giving two harvest windows.

directions: Black Genoa is a widely grown Italian heirloom producing purplish-black skinned fruit with deep amber-pink flesh and a rich, sweet flavor that many growers rank among the best dark-skinned figs for fresh eating. It is a reliably heavy producer of both an early breba crop on overwintered wood and a larger main crop on new growth, giving an extended summer-into-fall harvest in warm climates. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil and prune in winter to control size, since trees can become quite large and dense without management. Long popular in California and Australian home orchards, it performs well in Mediterranean and humid subtropical climates alike.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees or rooted cuttings in spring; Girkanets is grown primarily for its exceptional cold hardiness rather than fresh-market fruit size.

directions: Girkanets is a Central Asian pomegranate cultivar originating from the Caucasus and Turkmenistan region, valued in germplasm and breeding collections for its outstanding cold tolerance among fruiting pomegranates. It bears medium-sized, dark-red-skinned fruit with tart-sweet, juicy ruby arils that suit juicing and cooking more than fresh eating. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; established trees are extremely drought-tolerant and, like other cold-hardy Central Asian selections, can survive winter lows that would kill less hardy varieties such as Wonderful. It is a useful choice for gardeners at the colder edge of pomegranate-growing range who want insurance against occasional hard freezes.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root trees in late winter to spring in full sun and well-drained soil; expect the darkest fruit color to develop with full sun exposure through ripening.

directions: Sharp Velvet is a California selection prized for its very dark red-to-purple skin and deeply colored, soft-seeded arils with a rich sweet-tart flavor. The tree is vigorous and productive, bearing large fruit comparable in size to Wonderful but with a notably darker rind and juice, making it popular for fresh juicing where deep color is desired. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; it is drought-tolerant once established and, like most pomegranates, is self-fruitful and needs no pollinator. It suits warm-summer regions where fruit can fully color and sweeten before fall harvest.
